reading.identification: An early-15th-century "penshuisje" — one of the tiny tripe-sellers' houses attached to the flank of Ghent's Groot Vleeshuis on the Pensmarkt — a 5 m wide, gable-fronted dwelling in pale Balegem sandstone with a small commercial ground floor and a stepped gable to the street.
reading.notes:
EVIDENCE STATUS: no field is marked seen. Set B's magenta box lands on a timber palisade in the foreground, not on any building — the projection failed, so B contributes nothing about this facade and I refused to launder its neighbours' detail into this record. Set A resolves only massing: narrow gable-fronted unit, pale grey-white against pink-brick neighbours to the right, mid and lower facade occluded by foreground tile geometry. Everything below is derived from the identification.

HEIGHT: height_source is "no-data", so 9.0 m is a default. I have read it as apex-of-gable, giving 3.0 + 2.7 = 5.7 m to eaves and ~3.3 m of stepped gable above. If the generator instead treats 9.0 as eaves height, drop to the same 2 storeys and let the gable run to ~12 m rather than adding a third storey — a 25 m2 penshuisje is not a three-storey building.

MATERIAL: "marble" is the ITU-R P.2040 stone proxy, chosen for pale calcareous Balegem sandstone ashlar (eps ~6-7); it is not marble. Roughness 8 mm carries weathered ashlar with eroded joints in the 1-10 cm regime — do not mesh the coursing. Trim is the same stone (sills, drip courses, gable coping); window joinery is painted timber but I kept trim as stone because the trim material drives the ledge geometry, which here is masonry. FALLBACK: if the pale tone in A is limewash over brick rather than stone, switch wall to brick, roughness to 4.5 mm, trim to concrete — this is my main uncertainty and the reason confidence is 0.45.

GEOMETRY WORTH SPENDING ON (>10 cm, real facets at 28 GHz): the stepped gable itself — each step with its stone coping is a horizontal wedge and the dominant scatterer on the silhouette; deep window reveals at ~0.25 m in a 0.4-0.5 m masonry wall; projecting sills; one or two string courses across the gable front. These matter far more than anything on the wall plane.

DO NOT: put brick relief, joints or ornament into geometry. Do not give this building a flat top or a crowning cornice — a stepped gable has coping, not a kroonlijst.

CLUTTER: fronting street is a 0.9 m gravel tragel with car_access=none. Place NO vehicles on the Vleeshuistragel side. Appropriate clutter is pedestrian-scale on the Pensmarkt front: parked bikes against the wall, a bin, possibly a small cafe terrace; moss and staining at the base of the stone on the damp alley flank. The alley flank is a second frontage — it should be modelled as real wall with a few small openings, not as a blank party wall.

BEAM BUDGET: two street frontages, one of them 0.9 m from a walkable corridor, means the flank deserves near-equal detail to the front. The rear is not visible from either corridor and can be coarse.
